subject.title: [Feature]: Telegram — full agent activity visibility (Web UI parity)

question: Should Telegram gain a persistent per-step activity-message mode, and what disclosure, redaction, retention, and configuration policy should it use?
rationale: Current code already has transient progress drafts and durable verbose/reasoning surfaces, but turning every activity step into persistent Telegram messages changes privacy, security, transcript retention, and public config behavior that automation should not choose.

options.title: Design a redacted opt-in mode
options.body: Add a maintainer-approved default-off Telegram mode after specifying safe defaults, redaction rules, allowed step types, retention semantics, group/DM behavior, and live Telegram proof requirements.

options.title: Keep current preview and verbose surfaces
options.body: Leave Telegram on progress drafts plus /verbose and /reasoning controls, and close or defer the durable per-step message direction.

options.title: Create shared observer API first
options.body: Define a channel-safe observer/event API before adding Telegram-specific persistent rendering so Web UI, TUI, and Telegram activity views do not drift.

recommendation.title: Design a redacted opt-in mode
recommendation.body: Add a maintainer-approved default-off Telegram mode after specifying safe defaults, redaction rules, allowed step types, retention semantics, group/DM behavior, and live Telegram proof requirements.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest current-main ownership signal for Telegram progress, durable verbose behavior, and adjacent docs/code paths.
